title: `approve` takes the relayed yes and stops eliciting — the merge put the form back
description:
ADR 0057 (commit a2f1d6c) made `approve` take `confirmed: true` and deleted its `askYes` call. The merge commit c1066b4 resolved packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts badly and put the `askYes` block back into the `approve` handler (plan.ts ~lines 500–515, the 'Approve this brief?' prompt), while the schema and description still say the call itself is the human's yes. The tool now demands `confirmed: true` AND elicits a second time; in Claude Desktop the form never renders, the non-accept reads as a decline, and the human is told 'Not approved. Nothing was recorded.' `accept` (review.ts) and `decide` were merged correctly and are the model to follow.

Do: delete the `askYes` block and its two comments from `approve` in plan.ts so the handler goes straight to `approveBrief` — the same shape `accept` has. Keep `queued` (ADR 0056). Drop the `askYes` import only if `edit_decision` (plan.ts ~396) is not still using it — it is, so the import stays. The existing test 'a host with no elicitation approves on a relayed yes' in test/integration/mcp.test.ts is red on development today (expected 'ready', got 'needs-approval') and must go green; add nothing new unless a second test is needed to pin that `approve` never calls `elicitation/create` on a host that declares the capability (the `connect` client with a handler that records calls). Check `git diff a2f1d6c c1066b4 -- packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts` for anything else the merge dropped from ADR 0057 and restore it in the same change.

Out of scope: the elicitation-only remainder ADR 0057 lists (`edit_decision`, `run`'s overlap confirmation, `sync`, `team.ts`, `distribute.ts`) — they move when next touched.

brief.approach:
The merge commit c1066b4 put 13 lines back into the `approve` handler in packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts that ADR 0057 (commit a2f1d6c) had deleted: `git diff a2f1d6c c1066b4 -- packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts` shows exactly that block and nothing else. The tool's schema (`confirmed: z.literal(true)`) and description already say the call is the human's yes; only the body still asks a second time through `askYes`, and on a host whose elicitation does not render that reads as a decline.

1. In `registerPlanning`, in the `approve` handler (around plan.ts:500–515), delete the `askYes` call, its `if (!yes) return text('Not approved. Nothing was recorded.')`, and the two comment blocks above `queued` and above `askYes` — the ones starting "The human confirms one of two actions" and "One line. The approach and the criteria". Keep `const queued = queue ?? (await queueByDefault(paths))` and go straight to `approveBrief`, which is the shape `accept` in packages/mcp/src/tools/review.ts has. The `askYes` import stays: `edit_decision` (plan.ts ~396) still uses it, and ADR 0057 leaves that one where it is.

2. In test/integration/mcp.test.ts, next to 'a host with no elicitation approves on a relayed yes' (~line 352), add one test on the `connect` client (the one that declares elicitation) whose `human` callback throws or records: `approve` with `confirmed: true` must reach `ready` without the handler ever being called. That is the Desktop case — a host that claims the capability — and it is the one no existing test pins. Nothing else in the test file changes.

3. Do not touch `edit_decision`, `run`'s overlap confirmation in build.ts, `sync`, `team.ts` or `distribute.ts`: ADR 0057 names them as the elicitation-only remainder and they move when next touched.

acceptance.run: pnpm vitest run test/integration/mcp.test.ts -t "approves on a relayed yes"
acceptance.proves: The test that is red on development today goes green: a host with no elicitation capability approves a brief on `confirmed: true` and the node is `ready`.
Every approve path passes, including the new one: on a host that declares elicitation, `approve` never sends an `elicitation/create` request and still records the approval.
Exactly two hits — the import and the `edit_decision` call — so `approve` no longer elicits and the ADR 0057 remainder was left alone.
The whole integration suite is green, so removing the prompt broke no other flow that runs through `approve` (brief-then-run, rewrite-clears-approval, queue).
No unused import or dead branch was left behind after the deletion.
